_comment: Themes this extension adds on top of the seven Astryx ships.
Astryx has exactly seven themes — butter, chocolate, gothic, matcha,
neutral, stone, y2k — verified against packages/themes/ in the upstream
repository. These thirteen are OURS. They are built on Astryx's token
contract, carry the same token names and go through the same generator, so
a component cannot tell them apart; but they are not Meta's work and the
A seed is deliberately small. Everything not named here is inherited from
the neutral theme: the nine categorical hue ramps, the status colours and
the syntax palette are semantic categories rather than brand decisions, and
inheriting them means they keep the contrast behaviour the audit already
verified instead of thirteen new chances to get a badge wrong.
core.ink     darkest brand colour: accent, primary text, inverted surface
core.mid     secondary text — must reach 4.5:1 on core.paper
core.soft    disabled text, and the accent in dark mode
core.paper   page background in light mode
Fonts must come from the ten families sync-fonts.mjs already self-hosts;
a theme that needs an eleventh would add a download to every page.

themes.name: harbour
themes.label: Harbour
themes.description: Deep maritime navy with a cool grey page. The most conservative of the set — the one to reach for when a site has to look institutional.

themes.name: ember
themes.label: Ember
themes.description: Warm charcoal lit by a single ember orange. Reads as evening rather than alarm, and keeps the orange for the one thing that matters on the page.

themes.name: linen
themes.label: Linen
themes.description: A soft warm neutral built for long-form reading: low contrast between paper and surface, generous type, nothing competing with the text.

themes.name: orchid
themes.label: Orchid
themes.description: Muted purple with a cool paper. Distinctive without shouting, and the only theme in the set whose accent reads as decorative rather than corporate.

themes.name: cobalt
themes.label: Cobalt
themes.description: A saturated engineering blue on near-white. Built for dashboards and documentation, where a strong accent has to survive being repeated fifty times.

themes.name: moss
themes.label: Moss
themes.description: Deep forest green, quieter and colder than Astryx's own matcha. For organisations that want green without looking like a wellness brand.

themes.name: clay
themes.label: Clay
themes.description: Terracotta and warm stone. Earthy without being rustic, and the softest radius in the set so nothing has a hard corner.

themes.name: plum
themes.label: Plum
themes.description: Deep aubergine on a faintly warm page. Dark, adult and a little editorial — the theme for a publication rather than a product.

themes.name: sand
themes.label: Sand
themes.description: Desert warmth: pale ochre paper, dark umber ink. Bright without being white, which suits sites read outdoors or on cheap screens.

themes.name: ink
themes.label: Ink
themes.description: Near-black on white at the highest contrast the set offers. The one to pick when an accessibility statement has to survive scrutiny.

themes.name: lagoon
themes.label: Lagoon
themes.description: Blue-green water on pale sand. Fresher than Cobalt and warmer than Harbour, without tipping into turquoise.

themes.name: rose
themes.label: Rose
themes.description: Dusty rose, deliberately desaturated so it reads as considered rather than sweet. Pairs a serif heading with a plain body.

themes.name: graphite
themes.label: Graphite
themes.description: Cool monochrome with no hue at all in the brand colours. The neutral of last resort, for sites whose imagery has to supply every bit of colour.
